title: Oncall lag inspector and proactive downtime sentinel
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an oncall lag inspector service that surface alert ingestion and notification delivery latency heatmaps; introduces a configurable Downtime Sentinel that can proactively suppress noisy alerts during scheduled maintenance windows and surface mitigation hints to responders.
description:
Motivation: oncall teams have been seeing intermittent spikes in notification delivery latency that cause alert storms and noisy paging during downstream incidents. This PR introduces two cooperating features: (1) Oncall Lag Inspector -- lightweight streaming probe and analyzer that extracts per-route ingestion and delivery latency histograms and correlates them to backlog/consumer lag; (2) Downtime Sentinel -- a policy engine that detects scheduled or probable maintenance windows (from calendar metadata, release tags, and increased deploy surge signals) and can proactively tag or safely suppress non-actionable alerts while recommending runbook notes via incident-bot integration.

What this PR does (summary): implements a new slo-toolkit service (inspector) that subscribes to alert-transport metrics, computes rolling quantiles with adjustable windows, and emits compact heatmap metrics; adds a sentinel policy service that consumes those heatmaps plus deployment and calendar signals to generate 'downtime advisory' annotations and optional suppression decisions; integrates with incident-bot to attach suggested runbook lines and a short diagnostic checklist when a sentinel suppression is applied; adds dashboards and alerting rules to surface when the inspector itself is lagging.

Checklist: - [x] Core inspector probe and k-v config - [x] Downtime Sentinel policy engine with dry-run mode - [x] incident-bot annotation integration and playbook hint payload - [x] Backwards-compatible metrics names (prefixed slo_toolkit_inspector_) - [x] Unit and integration tests for quantile smoothing and policy decisions - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON and alert rules - [x] Docs: README and ops playbook entry - [x] Helm chart fragments and values examples

Commits (high level): - commit 1: "inspector: add streaming latency probe and quantile aggregator" -- introduces inspector binary, proto for compact heatmap events, unit tests for smoothing window. - commit 2: "sentinel: policy engine and dry-run annotations" -- implements policy evaluation pipeline, calendar and deploy signal adapters, incident-bot annotation hook, e2e integration test in CI. - commit 3: "ops: dashboard, helm values, docs and tests" -- adds Grafana JSON, helm values snippet, ops playbook, and fixes from review.

Files changed (high level): - src/inspector/collector.go (new) - src/inspector/quantiles.go (new) - src/sentinel/policy_engine.go (new) - integrations/incident-bot/annotation_hook.go (new) - charts/slo-toolkit/templates/sentinel.yaml (modified) - dashboards/inspector-heatmap.json (new) - test/integration/test_sentinel_e2e.go (new) - docs/oncall-lag-inspector.md (new)

Tests and CI: initial CI run reported a flaky test in test_inspector_smoothing (race on a timer). I reproduced locally, added a targeted synchronization and bump to the test harness timeout, then re-ran CI. Final CI summary: linter(pass), unit-tests(pass after rerun), integration(e2e) pass, helm-lint pass. The ci_status above reflects the final green state.

Review thread (highlights): - Arjun: asked for explanation on how the inspector avoids double-counting when multiple ingesters forward the same alert; suggested dedup by ingest_id and TTL. Maya: added dedup time-window and documented behavior; updated tests to assert no double-counting across replicas. - Lina: requested clearer opt-in paths for suppression and asked for a dry-run-only flag defaulting to true. Maya: implemented dry-run default=true and exposed an operator-facing flag `sentinel.suppressionMode=disabled|dry-run|enabled`. - Noah: flagged a performance concern for quantile window memory under high-cardinality routes; requested a fallback bucketization mode. Maya: added a 'bucketized' mode that reduces memory at the cost of resolution and added a benchmark in test/bench_inspector.go.

Operational notes and configuration: - default Helm values keep sentinel in dry-run with suppression disabled; to enable suppression set `sentinel.suppressionMode=enabled` and configure `sentinel.safeWindowMinutes` (default 15) and `sentinel.maxSuppressionDuration` (default 4h). - Inspector exposes metrics: slo_toolkit_inspector_latency_heatmap, slo_toolkit_inspector_probe_lag_seconds, slo_toolkit_inspector_probe_errors_total. - Incident-bot annotation payload includes: suggested runbook snippet, suggested rollback hints, and a brief diagnostic checklist (probe id, window, correlated deploy id). All annotation payloads are size-limited to 2KB and signed by the sentinel service key for auditability.

Backward compatibility and migration: uses new metric names with clear prefix; dashboards auto-detect when inspector metrics are absent and show instructions to enable the probe. No existing alerts are removed; default configs are conservative (dry-run) so immediate behavior change is avoided.

Post-merge follow-ups (tracked in ENG-9123): - Observability: add token-level cost estimate for inspector telemetry when sampling high-cardinality routes. - Policy tuning: add ML-driven threshold suggestions based on historical deploy patterns. - SRE runbook: add explicit steps for disabling sentinel suppression in emergency cases.

Merge: squashed and merged by Lina Gómez after approvals. Full merge message included links to the dashboard PR preview and the canary Helm chart values used in staging.

Notes for reviewers or operators: start with `helm upgrade --install slo-toolkit ./charts/slo-toolkit --set sentinel.suppressionMode=dry-run` in staging and monitor slo_toolkit_inspector_probe_lag_seconds and sentinel.advisory_count gauge for expected behavior. If you see unexpected suppression decisions, check `sentinel.trace_<probeid>` logs (log level debug) and file an SRE ticket with the trace id.
